title: Terms on the Host's Own Share of an Accepted Loss, Keyturn Host Protection Plan
content:
Under the Keyturn Host Protection Plan an accepted loss carries a share the host bears themselves, raised against the enrolment the claim was made under.

### Clauses no longer applied

> Retired clause: "Every accepted loss carries the host's own share, and that share is the deductible of the plan in force on the day of the loss rather than the plan in force on the day the claim is settled." This clause is no longer in force.

> Retired clause: "A host who has gone the plan's qualifying period without an accepted claim has the deductible reduced by the plan's claim-free discount, and a host who reaches the plan's waiver period has it waived entirely on the next accepted claim; the discount and the waiver do not stack, the waiver simply replacing the discount once it is earned." This clause is no longer in force.

Neither clause is applied to any share raised on an enrolment.

### Clauses in force

1. One deductible is raised for one loss however many kinds of damage the loss spans, and a loss that produces several repair invoices still carries one deductible.
2. Where the guest was found at fault the deductible is still raised against the host and then recovered from the guest, so the host's balance shows the charge and the recovery separately rather than netting to nothing.
3. No deductible is raised on a claim that is denied or withdrawn, and a deductible raised on a claim later denied is reversed in full.
4. A deductible is raised only while the enrolment is in the active, suspended or lapsed state, since a cancelled enrolment settles nothing further.

### The authority for clause 4

The standing of the enrolment is read from the enrolment record itself, for the enrolment the share is being raised on, before the share is raised; cover in force, cover paused and cover fallen away all admit a share, and cover ended by the host admits none.

### How claim-free months are measured

The months an enrolment has gone without an accepted claim are counted in whole calendar months from the claim-free day standing on the enrolment to the day the matter is handled.

### Points of judgement (hypothetical)

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| One loss damaging both the glass and the interior | One deductible, not two. |
| A loss where the guest was found at fault | The share is raised against the host, and the recovery from the guest is shown separately. |
| A claim refused after a share had been raised | The share is reversed in full. |

A host who has gone the plan's qualifying period without an accepted claim has the deductible reduced by the plan's claim-free discount, and a host who reaches the plan's waiver period has it waived entirely on the next accepted claim; the discount and the waiver do not stack, the waiver simply replacing the discount once it is earned.
